editorial.headline: Mung Bean Farming, Fully Open Nationally and Usable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01115 covers the full farming cycle for mung beans, including seed activity, with access across all business scales and no Bali PMA moratorium block.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01115 is a plain agricultural code, but not a narrow one. It covers mung bean farming as a complete field-to-post-harvest activity: land preparation, planting, maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest work when those steps form one integrated chain. The same scope also includes mung bean seed activity when it follows that same integrated agricultural cycle. In practical terms, this is not a code for a detached trading desk or an isolated processing business. Its center of gravity is cultivation, with post-harvest work included only where it remains part of the mung bean farming operation itself.

That scope matters because the record opens the activity across the full scale ladder: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. A local farmer, a small producer, a medium agribusiness, or a larger agricultural operator can all sit within this classification if the registered activity is genuinely mung bean farming and the post-harvest steps are part of the same farming sequence. The English reading should stay close to the Indonesian wording: this is agriculture for kacang hijau, including seed cultivation, not a general umbrella for every downstream mung bean product or commercial channel.

The national foreign-investment position is clean. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. There is no partial cap in the slim record, so the editorial conclusion should be equally direct: nationally, this activity is open to foreign-owned registration up to full foreign ownership. The source field is the investment-list reference, but the important operational point is the status and ceiling given in the record, not an invented layer of sectoral conditions.

The Bali picture is also clear, and it is better than many low-risk activities face on the island. Bali’s moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA registration island-wide, but this record marks KBLI 01115 as not blocked. The reason given is specific: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. That does not turn the code into a casual registration choice; it simply means the Bali-specific PMA block does not apply on the facts provided. The honest read is therefore straightforward: a foreigner can register this activity in Bali today under the record’s national openness and Bali status, provided the registered business is truly mung bean farming within this scope.
